title: Research
text:
My work sits at the intersection of psychiatry, sociology, and genetics.


01
Social connection
How social isolation and loneliness develop from childhood into adulthood, and how they intertwine with mental health.
See related papers ↓


02
Depression risk and presentation
Why depression looks different across age and sex, and how social, environmental, and genetic risk factors combine to shape symptoms across the life course.
See related papers ↓


03
Genetics and society
Bringing social science and genomics together responsibly.
See related papers ↓


04
Disparities in mental health
Understanding and reducing inequalities in mental health using existing longitudinal cohort data.
See related papers ↓

title: Katherine N Thompson, PhD
text:
I’m Katie, a Research Fellow in Population Mental Health based at the Centre for Longitudinal Studies, University College London (UCL) working as part of the fantastic Bridging Divides team.
I committed to open, diverse, and accessible science.
Co-founder and member of the Social Lives Collective and Responsible Genetics Collective.
Alum:

The Dunn Lab
The Wedow Lab
EDIT Lab







2026 – Present


Research Fellow, University College London (UCL)


Centre for Longitudinal Studies (CLS) – mentored by Dario Moreno Agostino


Researching gender inequalities in population mental health: mapping indicators of sexism within UK longitudinal cohorts, co-producing research with young people, and using causal inference to estimate the impact of sexism on depression and anxiety.




2024 – 2026


Postdoctoral Research Associate, Purdue University


Department of Sociology – mentored by Robbee Wedow and Erin Dunn


Developed pipelines for a data hub housing longitudinal cohorts including Add Health, WLS, HRS, UKB, MIDUS, and ELSA. Led a project using innovative mixed models to examine how systems contribute to depression symptoms, and a project using causal inference to test whether social connection mitigates disparities in depression symptoms.




2020 – 2023


PhD, Social, Genetic, and Developmental Psychiatry, King’s College London


Social Genetic and Developmental Psychiatry Centre, – Environmental Risk Longitudinal Twin Study (E-Risk), mentored by Louise Arseneault and Tim Matthews


Led three projects applying longitudinal methods to understand the link between social isolation and mental health problems across development, developing expertise in structural equation modelling, growth mixture modelling, cross-lagged panel models, and twin models.




2019 – 2020


Research Assistant, King’s College London


NIHR BioResource Centre Maudsley – GLAD Study, EDGI, and COPING Study, mentored by Gerome Breen


Managed NHS participant recruitment and trained around 200 NHS Trusts and services on recruitment strategies, and developed large-scale data management pipelines (N > 20,000) across multiple studies.




2016 – 2018


Research Assistant, King’s College London


Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology & Neuroscience – Early Development in Tuberous Sclerosis Study, mentored by Charlotte Tye


Conducted behavioural assessments in infants across the UK and in the Birkbeck Baby Lab, including eye tracking, the Mullen Scales of Early Learning, ADOS, and EEG.
